A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAMO and StructQA research. All 24 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable; text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of equations, figures, tables, and prose.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C report original TAMO experiments, including benchmark results, permutation robustness, ablations, efficiency measurements, and cross-dataset evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendix C, including the benchmark, ablation, and multi-table experiments.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same hypergraph encoder, alignment projector, combined structural and textual inputs, and autoregressive prediction procedure. The new HyperG discussion describes another method, not a modification to TAMO.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate StructQA, HiTab, WikiTQ, WikiSQL, and FeTaQA, plus MultiTabQA-geoQuery in Appendix C.7. Structural perturbation and cross-dataset scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including TAPAS and TAPEX in Table 5. HyperG is newly discussed but is not added to any reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, metrics, training settings, backbone configurations, and testing procedures remain identical. This includes the StructQA 60/20/20 split and the one-shot multi-table protocol in Appendix C.7.

E4.justification: The attention case study, permutation robustness tests, structural encoding analysis, efficiency analysis, token-count sensitivity, modality ablation, and transfer analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed statements in Appendix C.1. Checklist item 7 continues to state that repeated runs and error bars were not provided because of computational cost; no new uncertainty reporting appears.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative experimental findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains TAMO+SFT scores of 71.60 on StructQA and 85.90 on WikiSQL.

T1.justification: The task and hypergraph definitions, Equations 1–5, and mathematical reasoning about permutations are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: StructQA, treating tables as an independent modality, and TAMO's structural generalization benefits. The reported 42.65% average relative gain and central novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 qualifies the statement that competing methods 'all' require extensive pretraining to 'typically' and adds an explanation linking HyperG's augmentation pipeline to extra preparation beyond task-level supervision. TAMO's own limitations and interpretations of experimental results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information. The code and dataset access information is unchanged; the added HyperG reference supplies no new TAMO reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Huang et al. (2025), HyperG, to Section 4 and the bibliography. Appendix D.2 briefly describes its contextual augmentation and hypergraph learning pipeline and contrasts its preparation requirements with TAMO. Existing references and the broader positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the added citation, a short expansion of Appendix D.2, and the 'all' to 'typically' qualification. Section organization and the rest of the narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited paragraph and bibliography reflow on pages 9–14 and move Appendix D.3 lower on page 24. The arXiv margin stamp also changes. All figures and tables retain their content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional context by acknowledging HyperG and explaining its relationship to TAMO in Section 4 and Appendix D.2. It also makes the pretraining comparison less categorical. These are limited improvements in research positioning; the methods, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
